<h2 id="selectors-in-relationships">
	Selectors in Relationships
</h2>
<p>In Meshery, a selector is a way to specify which set of components a certain other component should affect or interact with. Selectors provide a flexible and powerful way to manage and orchestrate resources under Meshery&rsquo;s management.</p>
<p>Selectors can be applied to various components, enabling a wide range of relationship definitions. Here are some examples:</p>
<table class="table table-dark table-active">
    <tr>
        <th>Model Component</th>
        <th>Relationship Kind</th>
        <th>Relationship SubType</th>
        <th>Model Component</th>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Kubernetes ConfigMap</td>
        <td>Hierarchical</td>
        <td>Inventory</td>
        <td>Kubernetes Pod</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Kubernetes ConfigMap</td>
        <td>Hierarchical</td>
        <td>Inventory</td>
        <td>Kubernetes Deployment</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Meshery WASMFilter</td>
        <td>Hierarchical</td>
        <td>Inventory</td>
        <td>Istio EnvoyFilter</td>
    </tr>
</table>
<p>The above relationships pairs have hierarchical inventory relationships, and visual paradigm remain consistent across different components. A snippet of the selector backing this relationship is listed below.</p>
<details>
<summary>Example Relationship Selector</summary>
<code><pre>
"selector": {
    "allow": {
        "from": [
          {
            "kind": "ConfigMap",
            "model": "kubernetes",
            "patch": {
              "patchStrategy": "replace",
              "mutatorRef": [
                [
                  "name"
                ]
              ],
              "description": "In Kubernetes, ConfigMaps are a versatile resource that can be referenced by various other resources to provide configuration data to applications or other Kubernetes resources.\n\nBy referencing ConfigMaps in these various contexts, you can centralize and manage configuration data more efficiently, allowing for easier updates, versioning, and maintenance of configurations in a Kubernetes environment."
            }
          }
        ],
        "to": [
          {
            "kind": "Pod",
            "model": "kubernetes",
            "patch": {
              "patchStrategy": "replace",
              "mutatedRef": [
                [
                  "settings",
                  "spec",
                  "containers",
                  "_",
                  "envFrom",
                  "0",
                  "configMapRef",
                  "name"
                ]
              ],
              "description": "ConfigMaps can be referenced in the Pod specification to inject configuration data into the Pod's environment.\n\nThe keys from the ConfigMap will be exposed as environment variables to the container within the Pod."
            }
          }
        ]
    }
}
</pre></code>
</details>
<p>The above snippet defines a selector configuration for allowing relationships between <code>Kubernetes ConfigMap</code> and <code>Kubernetes Pod</code>.</p>
 <!-- add images -->
<h2 id="relationship-evaluation">
	Relationship Evaluation
</h2>
<p>Meshery employs a policy-driven approach to evaluate relationships between components. This evaluation helps in:</p>
<ul>
<li>Determining compatible components for establishing relationships</li>
<li>Suggesting potential relationships based on the current design</li>
<li>Validating existing relationships and identifying potential conflicts</li>
<li>Automating the configuration of components based on established relationships</li>
</ul>
<p>Each invocation of the evaluation process attempts to recursively evaluate the design until it reaches a stable state—i.e., no further changes are detected. If a bug in the evaluation policies causes non-terminating behavior (such as endlessly generating new components), the evaluation will be forcibly stopped after a configurable maximum depth (e.g., 5 iterations), and an error will be raised.</p>
<p>During evaluation, in addition to the input design, the evaluation engine has access to all relationships stored in the registry. These relationships serve as the source of truth for policies to validate existing relationships or identify new ones. Since relationships can be associated with different models, not all of them are relevant to a given design. To ensure efficiency, the evaluation process intelligently filters the registered relationships, retaining only those that directly impact the design.</p>
<p>Currently, the filtering logic includes only relationships from models that are already part of the design. For example, if the design consists solely of Kubernetes components, relationships from the AWS model will not be loaded for evaluation.</p>
<p>Beyond this automatic filtering, relationship evaluation can also be selectively disabled within the design. This is achieved by setting preferences to false for specific relationship categories, defined by their kind, type, and subtype.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="./images/relationship-evaluation-flow.svg" alt="Meshery Relationship"  /></p>
<h3 id="how-relationships-are-formed">
	How Relationships are formed?
</h3>
<ol>
<li>
<p>You can create relationships manually by using the edge handles, bringing related components to close proximity or dragging a component inside other component. It may happen that, you created a relationship from the UI, but the <a href='/concepts/logical/policies'>Policy Engine</a> rejected or overrode the decision if all the constraints for a particular relationship are not satisfied.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Relationships are automatically created when a component&rsquo;s configuration is modified in a way that relationship criteria is satisfied.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Explore an example relationship</div>
<p>To explore an example of this behavior, see the <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog/deployment/example-edge-permission-relationship-7dd39d30-7b14-4f9f-a66c-06ba3e5000fa.html">Example Edge-Permission Relationship</a> and follow the steps written in its description.</p>
</div>
<p>When the relationships are created by the user, almost in all cases the config of the involved components are patched. To see the specifics of patching refer <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/#patch-strategies">Patch Strategies</a>.</p>
<p>Designs are evaluated by the <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/policies/">Policy Engine</a> for potential relationships.</p>
<!-- Explain how and what configs get patched when relationships are created -->
<!-- Explain real time evaluation of relationships on -->

<!-- 2. When compoennt config is update and it satisfied the condition for the relationship -->
<h3 id="patch-strategies">
	Patch Strategies
</h3>
<p>Patches in Meshery relationships utilize strategies and references (mutatorRef/mutatedRef) for the from and to fields. These convey the property path that will be updated as the relationship is created.</p>
<h3 id="caveats-and-considerations">
	Caveats and Considerations
</h3>
<ol>
<li>If the user creates a <code>Hierarchical Inventory</code> relationship between <code>Pod</code>, <code>Job</code>, and any other high-level Kubernetes resources like <code>Deployment</code>, <code>StatefulSet</code>, or <code>CronJobs</code>, after the relationship has been established unfortunately, there&rsquo;s no system to remove the extra pod configuration automatically.
If the design is not configured with <code>labels</code> <code>selectors</code> and <code>replicas</code> appropriately, there&rsquo;s a possibility of additional resources getting provisioned when deployed. e.g., The relationship between a Pod and deployment can result in 2 Pods (1 pod coming as part of deployment resource) and 1 Deployment.  It&rsquo;s important to be aware of this possibility and manage configurations carefully to avoid unexpected issues during deployment</li>
</ol>
<h1 id="itemizing-your-relationship-definitions-in-your-meshery-deployment">
	Itemizing your Relationship Definitions in your Meshery deployment
</h1>
<p>In any given Meshery deployment, you can reference and search the full set of registered relationships (in Meshery&rsquo;s internal registry) using either of Meshery&rsquo;s client interfaces.</p>
<p><strong>Meshery UI</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Visit <em>Settings</em> &ndash;&gt; <em>Registry</em></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Meshery CLI</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Run <code>mesheryctl relationship list</code></li>
</ul>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Workspaces</h1>
          
          <p>Like a Google Drive, Meshery Workspaces serve as a virtual space for your team-based work. Create a Workspace to organize your work and to serve as the central point of collaboration for you and your teams and a central point of access control to Environments and their resources.</p>
<p>You may create Workspaces to organize project-based work or to create domains of responsibility for your teams or segregate Designs and Environments and track team activity.</p>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Your team collaboration point</div>
<p>Workspaces facilitate collaboration between you and your teams, allow you to control access to resources, and track activity and report on related events.</p>
</div>
<h2 id="key-features">
	Key Features
</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Resource Sharing</strong> Workspaces allow for seamless resource sharing among team members, fostering collaboration.</li>
<li><strong>Logical Grouping</strong> Within Workspaces, you can group related components such as environments and infrastructure designs.</li>
<li><strong>Flexibility</strong>: Workspaces support various resources like Kubernetes, Prometheus, Jaeger, Nginx, and more.</li>
<li><strong>Simplified Management</strong> Managing and deploying resources is made easy within Workspaces.</li>
<li><strong>Access Control</strong> Workspaces allow you to control access to resources by granting permissions to users and teams.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="workspace-relationships-and-restrictions">
	Workspace Relationships and Restrictions
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Access to Workspaces may be granted to one or more teams.</li>
<li>As a point of collaboration to facilitate work, Workspaces may have zero or more Environments associated.</li>
</ul>
<p>After creating a Workspace, of your next steps is to resource that Workspace. Like a shared drive (or or shared collection of files). Workspaces are your Google Drive, while Meshery Designs are your Google Docs.</p>
<h2 id="key-components">
	Key Components
</h2>
<h3 id="environments">
	Environments
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Environments are a central part of a workspace. They serve as a logical grouping for managing connections. A connection, in this context, can be either managed or discovered by Meshery. Examples of connections include Kubernetes clusters, Prometheus instances, Jaeger traces, Nginx servers, and more.</li>
<li>One or more environments can be assigned to a workspace.</li>
<li>Same environment can be assigned to multiple workspaces.</li>
</ul>
<p>See &ldquo;<a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/environments/">Environments</a>&rdquo; section for more information.</p>
<h3 id="designs">
	Designs
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Infrastructure Designs are essential for creating reusable deployment templates. Users belonging to teams with access to a workspace can utilize these designs to deploy resources in the Kubernetes clusters associated with that workspace.</li>
<li>Like a shared drive (or or shared collection of files), Workspaces are your Google Drive, while Meshery Designs are your Google Docs.</li>
<li>One ore more designs can be assigned to a workspace.</li>
<li>Same design can be assigned to multiple workspaces.</li>
</ul>
<p>See &ldquo;<a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/designs/">Meshery Designs</a>&rdquo; section for more information.</p>
<h3 id="organizations">
	Organizations
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Organizationa are the unit of tenancy in Meshery. Organizations group users together.</li>
<li>Organizations own all resources created by users, like Workspaces, Designs, Environments, and so on.</li>
<li>Remote Providers can extend Meshery to include additional identity and user management features like heirarchical organizations, or teams (as user groups), and so on.</li>
<li>Remote Providers can extend Meshery to offer fine-grained permissions and access control to resources like Workspaces, Designs, Environments, and so on.</li>
</ul>
<p>Learn more about <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/authorization/">extensible authorization</a>.</p>
 <!-- "[Organizations](/extensions/team-management)" section for more information. -->
<!-- ### Teams

- A Workspace is closely associated with Teams in Meshery. Teams are groups of users with varying permissions, and they are at the center of resource access and management within a Workspace.
- One ore more teams can be assigned to a workspace.
- Same team can be assigned to multiple workspaces.

See "[Teams](/extensions/team-management)" section for more information. -->
<h3 id="connections">
	Connections
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Connections in Meshery refer to various resources that can be either managed or unmanaged, but are discovered and made accessible for use. Examples of Connections include Kubernetes clusters, Prometheus instances, Jaeger services, Nginx deployments, and more. These Connections serve as a fundamental part of Workspaces, as users can deploy infrastructure designs within the context of these Connections.</li>
<li>Connections can be assigned to one or more environments.</li>
<li>Same connection can be assigned to multiple environments.</li>
</ul>
<p>See &ldquo;<a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/connections/">Connections</a>&rdquo; section for more information.</p>
<h2 id="best-practices">
	Best Practices
</h2>
<p>To make the most of Meshery Workspaces, here are some best practices:</p>
<ul>
<li>Clearly define permissions in the form of team assignement to ensure proper access control.</li>
<li>Use Infrastructure Designs to standardize resource deployments.</li>
<li>Regularly review and update your Workspace&rsquo;s resources and configurations.</li>
</ul>
<p>Meshery Workspaces enhance collaboration within your teams, providing a structured environment for sharing and managing resources. By following best practices and understanding the core components of Workspaces, you can maximize the benefits of this feature in Meshery.</p>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Extensibility: APIs</h1>
          
          <h2 id="mesherys-apis">
	Meshery&rsquo;s APIs
</h2>
<p>Each of Meshery&rsquo;s APIs are subject to the following authentication and authorization system. The REST and GraphQL APIs are available on the same network port you use to connect to Meshery UI, which is <code>9081/tcp</code> by default. Each of the API endpoints are exposed through <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/router/server.go">server.go</a>. Endpoints are grouped by function (e.g. <code>/api/system/version</code>). Additionally, <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/providers/">Remote Providers</a> can extend Meshery&rsquo;s endpoints behind the <code>/api/extensions/</code> endpoint.</p>
<h3 id="api-reference">
	API Reference
</h3>
<div class="tab-container">
  <!-- Tab 1: REST API -->
  <input id="tab1" type="radio" name="tabs" checked>
  <label for="tab1" data-icon="&#xf1cb;">REST API</label>
  <section class="tabbed" id="content1">
    <p>Meshery Server's REST API is available at <code>[hostname]:[port]/api/</code>.</p>
    <div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Meshery's REST API Reference</div>
<p>See <a href="/v0.9/reference/rest-apis/">REST API Reference</a> Self-generated API documentation for Meshery&rsquo;s REST API. Documentation is generated from Meshery&rsquo;s Open API schema.
</div></p>
  </section>
  <!-- Tab 2: GraphQL API -->
  <input id="tab2" type="radio" name="tabs">
  <label for="tab2" data-icon="&#xf17d;">GraphQL API</label>
  <section class="tabbed" id="content2">
    <p>Meshery Server's GraphQl API is available at <code>{hostname]:[port]/api/graphql/query</code>. A GraphQL request can be made as a POST request to the endpoint with the query as the payload. Meshery Server's GraphQL API can be used to perform three operations:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Queries for data retrieval.</li>
      <li>Mutations for creating, updating, and deleting data.</li>
      <li>Subscriptions for watching for any data changes.</li>
    </ul>
    <p>Explore the Meshery GraphQL API using the interactive Playground provided with Meshery instance at http://localhost:9081/api/system/graphql/playground.</p>
    <div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Meshery's GraphQL API Reference</div>
<p>See <a href="/v0.9/reference/graphql-apis/">GraphQL API Reference</a> Self-generated API documentation for Meshery&rsquo;s GraphQL API. The API can be explored interactively using the GraphQL Playground. Documentation is generated from Meshery&rsquo;s GraphQL schema. Each table below documents a GraphQL type.
</div></p>
  </section>
</div>
<h3 id="authentication">
	Authentication
</h3>
<p>Requests to any of the API endpoints must be authenticated and include a valid JWT access token in the HTTP headers. Type of authentication is determined by the selected <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/api/#providers">Provider</a>. Use of the Local Provider, &ldquo;None&rdquo;, puts Meshery into single-user mode and does not require authentication.</p>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">What are authentication tokens?</div>
<p>Meshery authentication tokens allow users or systems to authenticate with Meshery Server via either its two clients, <a href="/v0.9/reference/mesheryctl/">Meshery CLI</a> and <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/api/#how-to-get-your-token">UI</a>, or its two APIs: <a href="/v0.9/reference/rest-apis/">REST</a> or <a href="/v0.9/reference/graphql-apis/">GraphQL</a>.</p>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s authentication token system provide secure access to Meshery&rsquo;s powerful management features.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="how-to-get-your-token">
	How to get your token
</h3>
<p>There are two ways to get your authentication token:</p>
<ol>
<li>Meshery UI</li>
<li>Meshery CLI</li>
</ol>
<p>Using Meshery UI, you can get a copy of your authentication token by following these steps:</p>
<ol>
<li>Log into Meshery by selecting your identity provider of choice (typically found at <code>http:&lt;meshery-server&gt;:9081/provider</code>)</li>
<li>Navigate to your user&rsquo;s avatar in the upper lefthand corner and select &ldquo;Get Token&rdquo; from the dropdown of profile section.</li>
</ol>
<p>Using Meshery CLI, you can get a copy of your authentication token by executing this command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system login</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>In order to use this command, you must have a web browser available on your system (this command cannot be executed on a headless system).</p>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">How to use the token for requests to Meshery Rest API using API clients</div>
<p>Download your token from Meshery UI and copy the token value from the downloaded file, this will be used for authentication.</p>
</div>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">meshery-provider: Meshery
token: your token</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert">
<p>Navigate to the cookies section your API testing platform, to set the appropriate name and value for the cookie, then make sure to save the configured cookies to initiate the request.</p>
<p>The request will be sent to the Meshery API using the configured cookies for authentication.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="endpoints">
	Endpoints
</h3>
<p>Each of the API endpoints are exposed through <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/router/server.go">server.go</a>. Endpoints are grouped by function (e.g. <code>/api/mesh</code> or <code>/api/perf</code>).</p>
<p>Alternatively, <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/providers/">Remote Providers</a> can extend Meshery&rsquo;s endpoints behind the <code>/api/extensions/</code> endpoint.</p>
<h2 id="authorization">
	Authorization
</h2>
<p>While Meshery only requires a valid token in order to allow clients to invoke its APIs, Remote Providers can optionally enforce key-based permissions.</p>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Extensibility: Authorization</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery features an extensible authorization system that offers the ability to deliver fine-grained access control across it&rsquo;s web-based user interface, <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/">Meshery UI</a>.</p>
<h2 id="authorization-keys">
	Authorization Keys
</h2>
<p>The extensible authorization system consists of a large set of keys. Each key uniquely represents a specific capability, for example, the ability to view a <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/connections/">Connection</a>, edit or delete a Connection. With the help of these keys, the system evaluates the permissions during runtime and renders UI both helping offer a secure management system and a customizable user experience.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Note</div>
<p>The extensible authorization system is available to both Local and Remote Providers. Depending upon your chosen <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/providers/">Remote Provider</a>, keys, clustering of them, assigning them to user groups, not just individual users or to user roles may be offered.</p>
</div>
<h2 id="authorization-framework">
	Authorization Framework
</h2>
<p>Meshery utilizes CASL (JS-based permission framework) to evaluate any given user&rsquo;s set of session keys against the built-in keyhooks populated through each invidual Meshery UI page. This allows for granular control over the UI, empowering you to tailor your Meshery experience to your organization&rsquo;s needs by limiting access to specific features and functionalities based on the user&rsquo;s assigned keys.</p>
<a href="./images/permission-in-UI.png">
  <img style="width:min(100%,800px)" src="./images/permission-in-UI.png" />
</a>
<h3 id="introduction-to-casljs">
	Introduction to CASL.js
</h3>
<p><a href="https://casl.js.org">CASL.js</a> is an isomorphic authorization JavaScript library which restricts what resources a given client is allowed to access. It&rsquo;s designed to be incrementally adoptable and can easily scale between a simple claim based and fully featured subject and attribute based authorization. It makes it easy to manage and share permissions/keys across UI components, API services, and database queries.</p>
<p>An example of how CASL evaluate permission in UI.


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">&lt;React.Fragment&gt;
	{!CAN(keys.DELETE_CONNECTION.action, keys.DELETE_CONNECTION.subject) &amp;&amp; (
		&lt;Button id=&#34;delete-connection&#34;&gt;Delete&lt;Button/&gt;
	)}
&lt;/React.Fragment&gt;</code>
	</div>
</pre>
</p>
<p>Once a user has logged in, the backend will send a response with the permissions that the user has. Those permissions will be used to create abilities on the frontend, CASL gets updated with those abilities. The UI maintains a constant file containing all allowed permissions, referred to as keys. With the help of these keys, CAN function evaluates the permissions during runtime and renders UI.</p>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Note</div>
<p>It&rsquo;s important to understand not all pages uses CASL authorization, means even if you are not assigned with any role within organization you might access preferences page and Meshery UI dashboard.</p>
</div>
<h2 id="authorization-using-local-provider">
	Authorization using Local Provider
</h2>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s built-in identity provider, &ldquo;Local&rdquo; Provider, operates with a large set of predefined keys interspersed throughout Meshery UI and persisted in <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/database/">Meshery Database</a>. These keys are used to evaluate the permissions of a given user and render the UI accordingly. The keys are grouped into three categories: <code>action</code>, <code>subject</code>, and <code>object</code>.</p>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert">
  <h4 class="alert-heading">Discussion Forum</h4>
  <p>Don't find an answer to your question here? Ask on the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">Discussion Forum</a>.</p>
</div>


        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Extensibility: Build-time</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery supports build-time extensibility, allowing system integrators to customize the Meshery container image during the Docker build process. This extension point enables organizations to inject custom configurations, data, provider extensions, and other resources directly into the Meshery container image at build-time.</p>
<h2 id="build-time-extension-point">
	Build-time Extension Point
</h2>
<p>The build-time extension point allows you to supply custom content by placing a <code>.meshery</code> directory at the root of the Meshery repository before building the Docker image. The contents of this directory will be copied into the container image and made available to Meshery at runtime.</p>
<h3 id="how-it-works">
	How It Works
</h3>
<ol>
<li><strong>Placement</strong>: Create a <code>.meshery</code> directory at the root of the Meshery repository (same level as the <code>Dockerfile</code>).</li>
<li><strong>Content</strong>: Add any build-time configuration, data, packages, or other resources you want to include in the container image to this directory.</li>
<li><strong>Build</strong>: Run <code>docker build</code> as usual. The Docker build process will automatically copy the <code>.meshery</code> directory and its contents into the container image at <code>/home/appuser/.meshery/</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Runtime Access</strong>: The injected content will be available to Meshery at runtime under <code>/home/appuser/.meshery/</code>.</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="directory-structure">
	Directory Structure
</h3>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>meshery/                     # Repository root
├── .meshery/               # Build-time extension directory (optional)
│   ├── config/            # Custom configuration files
│   ├── provider/          # Provider-specific extensions
│   ├── content/           # Custom patterns, filters, applications
│   └── ...                # Any other custom content
├── install/
│   └── docker/
│       └── Dockerfile     # Main Dockerfile
└── ...
</code></pre><h3 id="example-use-cases">
	Example Use Cases
</h3>
<h4 id="custom-configuration-files">
	Custom Configuration Files
</h4>
<p>Place custom configuration files that should be bundled with your Meshery deployment:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">mkdir -p .meshery/config
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">&#34;custom_setting=value&#34;</span> &gt; .meshery/config/custom.conf
</span></span></code></pre></div><h4 id="provider-specific-extensions">
	Provider-specific Extensions
</h4>
<p>Include proprietary or organization-specific provider extensions:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">mkdir -p .meshery/provider/MyProvider/v1.0.0
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">cp /path/to/provider-extension.tar.gz .meshery/provider/MyProvider/v1.0.0/
</span></span></code></pre></div><h4 id="custom-content">
	Custom Content
</h4>
<p>Add organization-specific patterns, filters, or applications:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">mkdir -p .meshery/content/patterns
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">cp /path/to/custom-patterns/* .meshery/content/patterns/
</span></span></code></pre></div><h4 id="pre-installed-models">
	Pre-installed Models
</h4>
<p>Include pre-downloaded models or manifests that might not be available at runtime:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">mkdir -p .meshery/models
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">cp -r /path/to/custom-models/* .meshery/models/
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="building-with-build-time-extensions">
	Building with Build-time Extensions
</h3>
<p>To build a Meshery container image with your custom build-time extensions:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Create your .meshery directory with custom content</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">mkdir -p .meshery/config
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">&#34;my_config=value&#34;</span> &gt; .meshery/config/custom.conf
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Build the Docker image (from the repository root)</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">docker build -f install/docker/Dockerfile -t meshery:custom .
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>The build process will:</p>
<ol>
<li>Copy all files from the build context (including <code>.meshery</code> directory)</li>
<li>Extract the <code>.meshery</code> directory in a build stage</li>
<li>Copy the <code>.meshery</code> directory contents to <code>/home/appuser/.meshery/</code> in the final image</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="runtime-behavior">
	Runtime Behavior
</h3>
<p>At runtime, Meshery will have access to:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Seed Content</strong>: <code>/home/appuser/.meshery/seed_content/</code> (standard Meshery seed content)</li>
<li><strong>Config</strong>: <code>/home/appuser/.meshery/config/</code> (Meshery configuration files)</li>
<li><strong>Custom Content</strong>: Any additional content you placed in <code>.meshery/</code> during build</li>
</ul>
<p>Your custom content in <code>.meshery/</code> will be merged with the standard Meshery directories. The contents are owned by the <code>appuser</code> user in the container.</p>
<h3 id="important-notes">
	Important Notes
</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Optional</strong>: The <code>.meshery</code> directory is optional. If not present during build, the Docker build will continue without errors.</li>
<li><strong>Merge Behavior</strong>: If you create subdirectories with the same names as existing Meshery directories (e.g., <code>config</code>), the contents will be merged.</li>
<li><strong>Permissions</strong>: All files copied from the build-time <code>.meshery</code> directory will be owned by <code>appuser:appuser</code> in the container.</li>
<li><strong>Not in Version Control</strong>: The <code>.meshery</code> directory at the repository root is typically not committed to version control. Add it to <code>.gitignore</code> if you&rsquo;re creating temporary build-time extensions.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="security-considerations">
	Security Considerations
</h3>
<p>When using build-time extensions:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Review Content</strong>: Always review the contents of the <code>.meshery</code> directory before building to ensure no sensitive information or malicious content is included.</li>
<li><strong>Secrets Management</strong>: Do not include secrets, passwords, or API keys in the build-time <code>.meshery</code> directory. Use environment variables or runtime configuration for sensitive data.</li>
<li><strong>Trust Sources</strong>: Only include content from trusted sources to avoid introducing security vulnerabilities.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="comparison-with-runtime-extension-points">
	Comparison with Runtime Extension Points
</h3>
<p>Meshery supports multiple <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/">extension points</a> at different stages:</p>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Extension Point</th>
          <th>When</th>
          <th>Use Case</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td><strong><a href="/v0.9/extensibility/build-time/">Build-time</a></strong></td>
          <td>During <code>docker build</code></td>
          <td>Pre-package custom configurations, offline packages, proprietary plugins</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong><a href="/v0.9/extensibility/">Boot-time</a></strong></td>
          <td>Container startup</td>
          <td>Dynamic configuration that can change between deployments</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong><a href="/v0.9/extensibility/">Runtime</a></strong></td>
          <td>While Meshery is running</td>
          <td>User-installed plugins, dynamically loaded extensions</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Choose the build-time extension point when you need to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Bundle organization-specific customizations in a custom container image</li>
<li>Include content that must be available before Meshery starts</li>
<li>Create a self-contained deployment with all dependencies pre-packaged</li>
<li>Deploy in air-gapped or restricted network environments</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="troubleshooting">
	Troubleshooting
</h3>
<p><strong>My <code>.meshery</code> directory isn&rsquo;t being copied</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Ensure the directory is at the repository root (same level as <code>install/docker/Dockerfile</code>)</li>
<li>Check that the directory isn&rsquo;t excluded in <code>.dockerignore</code></li>
<li>Verify the build context includes the repository root</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Permission denied errors at runtime</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The build process should automatically set ownership to <code>appuser:appuser</code></li>
<li>If issues persist, check file permissions in your source <code>.meshery</code> directory</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Build fails with &ldquo;no such file or directory&rdquo;</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>This should not happen as the <code>.meshery</code> directory is optional</li>
<li>If you see this error, check your Docker version and build logs</li>
</ul>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Extensibility</h1>
          
          
<p>Meshery has an extensible architecture with several different types of extension points.</p>
<h2 id="extension-points">
	Extension Points
</h2>
<p>Meshery is not just an application. It is a set of microservices where the central component is itself called Meshery. Integrators may extend Meshery by taking advantage of designated Extension Points. Extension points come in various forms and are available through Meshery’s architecture.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="./images/meshery_extension_points.svg" alt="Meshery Extension Points"  /></p>
<p><em>Figure: Extension points available throughout Meshery</em></p>
<h2 id="list-of-extensions">
	List of Extensions
</h2>
<p>A browsable collection of various Meshery extensions is available at <a href="https://meshery.io/extensions">https://meshery.io/extensions</a>.</p>
<h2 id="types-of-extension-points">
	Types of Extension Points
</h2>
<p>The following points of extension are currently incorporated into Meshery.</p>
<ul style="margin:0;"> 
    <li style="list-style-type: inherit; margin: 0"><a href="/extensions/adapters">Extensibility: Meshery Adapters</a> - Meshery architecture is extensible. Meshery provides several extension points for working with different cloud native infrastructure via <a href="/extensions/adapters">adapters</a>, <a href="/extensibility/load-generators">load generators</a> and <a href="/extensibility/providers">providers.</a></li>
</ul>


<ul class="section-title">

  

  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/verify-compatibility/">Ensuring Extension Compatibility with Meshery</a>

        
          - A guide for Meshery extension developers on maintaining compatibility with the Meshery platform, covering shared frameworks, dependencies, and build tooling.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/api/">Extensibility: APIs</a>

        
          - Meshery architecture is extensible, offering an array of extension points and REST and GraphQL APIs.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/authorization/">Extensibility: Authorization</a>

        
          - Meshery architecture is extensible. Meshery provides several extension points for working with different cloud native projects via authorization, adapters, load generators and providers.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/build-time/">Extensibility: Build-time</a>

        
          - System integrators can supply build-time configuration, data, packages, and other extensions to Meshery&#39;s container image.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/load-generators/">Extensibility: Load Generators</a>

        
          - Meshery offers support for more types of Kubernetes and cloud native infrastructure than any other project or product in the world. Meshery uses adapters for more deeply managing specific types of infrastructure.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/providers/">Extensibility: Providers</a>

        
          - Meshery uses providers to enrich the level of depth by which it manages cloud native infrastructure.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/ui/">Extensibility: UI</a>

        
          - Meshery offers support for more adapters than any other project or product in the world. Meshery UI has a number of extension points that allow users to customize their experience with third-party plugins.
        
      </li>
    
  

</ul>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" standalone="yes"?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">
  <channel>
    <title>Extensibility on Documentation</title>
    <link>/v0.9/extensibility/</link>
    <description>Recent content in Extensibility on Documentation</description>
    <generator>Hugo</generator>
    <language>en</language>
    <atom:link href="/v0.9/extensibility/index.xml" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml" />
    <item>
      <title>Ensuring Extension Compatibility with Meshery</title>
      <link>/v0.9/extensibility/verify-compatibility/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/extensibility/verify-compatibility/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;The Meshery ecosystem is designed for extensibility, with the core platform (&lt;code&gt;meshery/meshery&lt;/code&gt;) providing extension points for a variety of plugins, collectively managed in the &lt;code&gt;meshery-extensions&lt;/code&gt; GitHub organization. To ensure a stable and seamless user experience, it is critical that extensions remain compatible with the Meshery platform, especially when shared frameworks or dependencies are updated.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This guide outlines the key areas of compatibility and provides a general process for extension developers to follow when Meshery&amp;rsquo;s underlying frameworks are updated.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Extensibility: APIs</title>
      <link>/v0.9/extensibility/api/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/extensibility/api/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2 id=&#34;mesherys-apis&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Meshery&amp;rsquo;s APIs&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Each of Meshery&amp;rsquo;s APIs are subject to the following authentication and authorization system. The REST and GraphQL APIs are available on the same network port you use to connect to Meshery UI, which is &lt;code&gt;9081/tcp&lt;/code&gt; by default. Each of the API endpoints are exposed through &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/router/server.go&#34;&gt;server.go&lt;/a&gt;. Endpoints are grouped by function (e.g. &lt;code&gt;/api/system/version&lt;/code&gt;). Additionally, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/extensibility/providers/&#34;&gt;Remote Providers&lt;/a&gt; can extend Meshery&amp;rsquo;s endpoints behind the &lt;code&gt;/api/extensions/&lt;/code&gt; endpoint.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;api-reference&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;API Reference&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;tab-container&#34;&gt;&#xA;  &lt;!-- Tab 1: REST API --&gt;&#xA;  &lt;input id=&#34;tab1&#34; type=&#34;radio&#34; name=&#34;tabs&#34; checked&gt;&#xA;  &lt;label for=&#34;tab1&#34; data-icon=&#34;&amp;#xf1cb;&#34;&gt;REST API&lt;/label&gt;&#xA;  &lt;section class=&#34;tabbed&#34; id=&#34;content1&#34;&gt;&#xA;    &lt;p&gt;Meshery Server&#39;s REST API is available at &lt;code&gt;[hostname]:[port]/api/&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Extensibility: Authorization</title>
      <link>/v0.9/extensibility/authorization/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/extensibility/authorization/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery features an extensible authorization system that offers the ability to deliver fine-grained access control across it&amp;rsquo;s web-based user interface, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/architecture/&#34;&gt;Meshery UI&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;authorization-keys&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Authorization Keys&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The extensible authorization system consists of a large set of keys. Each key uniquely represents a specific capability, for example, the ability to view a &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/connections/&#34;&gt;Connection&lt;/a&gt;, edit or delete a Connection. With the help of these keys, the system evaluates the permissions during runtime and renders UI both helping offer a secure management system and a customizable user experience.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Extensibility: Build-time</title>
      <link>/v0.9/extensibility/build-time/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/extensibility/build-time/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery supports build-time extensibility, allowing system integrators to customize the Meshery container image during the Docker build process. This extension point enables organizations to inject custom configurations, data, provider extensions, and other resources directly into the Meshery container image at build-time.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;build-time-extension-point&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Build-time Extension Point&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The build-time extension point allows you to supply custom content by placing a &lt;code&gt;.meshery&lt;/code&gt; directory at the root of the Meshery repository before building the Docker image. The contents of this directory will be copied into the container image and made available to Meshery at runtime.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Extensibility: Load Generators</title>
      <link>/v0.9/extensibility/load-generators/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/extensibility/load-generators/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Users may prefer to use one load generator over the next given the difference of capabilities between load generators, so Meshery provides a &lt;code&gt;load generator interface&lt;/code&gt; (a gRPC interface) behind which a load generator can be implemented. Meshery provides users with choice of which load generator they prefer to use for a given performance test. Users may configure their own preference for the load generator, different from the default load generator.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Extensibility: Providers</title>
      <link>/v0.9/extensibility/providers/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/extensibility/providers/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery offers &lt;em&gt;Providers&lt;/em&gt; as a point of extensibility. It has a built-in Local Provider, named &lt;strong&gt;&amp;ldquo;None&amp;rdquo;&lt;/strong&gt; and supports &lt;em&gt;Remote Providers&lt;/em&gt; that are designed to be pluggable. &lt;em&gt;Remote Providers&lt;/em&gt; offer a point of extension to users / integrators to deliver enhanced functionality such as authentication and authorization, using Meshery as a platform.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Extensibility points offer clean separation of Meshery&amp;rsquo;s core functionality versus plugin functionality.&lt;/strong&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;See a list of &lt;a href=&#34;https://meshery.io/extensions&#34;&gt;Meshery&amp;rsquo;s extensions&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Remote Providers should be able to offer custom RBAC, custom UI components, and custom backend components&lt;/strong&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Dynamically loadable frameworks need to be identified or created to serve each of these purposes.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;what-functionality-do-providers-offer&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;What functionality do Providers offer?&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The functionalities offerred by a &lt;em&gt;Remote Provider&lt;/em&gt; may vary broadly between providers. Meshery offers extension points that Remote Providers are able to use to inject various functionalities, functionalities that are specific to that provider.&#xA;Some examples include:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Extensibility: UI</title>
      <link>/v0.9/extensibility/ui/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/extensibility/ui/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery UI has a number of extension points that allow you to greatly customize both its functional behavior and visual appearance. These extension points come in different types, and this document describes each type, its example use, best practices to consider, and caveats of which to be aware.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;extensibility-customizing-text-based-forms-using-rjsf-custom-component&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Extensibility: Customizing Text-based Forms using RJSF Custom Component&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;RJSFWrapperComponent provides customizations for RJSF forms, overriding the default behavior of meshery-ui rjsf forms. The &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L66&#34;&gt;Rjsf forms are wrapped&lt;/a&gt; in this component to receive custom props from a Meshery extension.&#xA;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&#x9;&lt;code class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;&amp;lt;RJSFWrapperComponent {...props}&amp;gt;&#xA;  &amp;lt;RJSFForm&#xA;    isLoading={isLoading}&#xA;    schema={schema}&#xA;    data={data}&#xA;    onChange={(e) =&amp;gt; {&#xA;      setData(e.formData)&#xA;    }}&#xA;    jsonSchema={jsonSchema}&#xA;  /&amp;gt;&#xA;&amp;lt;/RJSFWrapperComponent&amp;gt;&lt;/code&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&#xA;See this &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L91&#34;&gt;RJSF Component&lt;/a&gt; as an example of how these properties are received.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
  </channel>
</rss>

# meshery/meshery / docs/static/v0.9/extensibility/integrations/accurate/index.html

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Extensibility: Load Generators</h1>
          
          <p>Users may prefer to use one load generator over the next given the difference of capabilities between load generators, so Meshery provides a <code>load generator interface</code> (a gRPC interface) behind which a load generator can be implemented. Meshery provides users with choice of which load generator they prefer to use for a given performance test. Users may configure their own preference for the load generator, different from the default load generator.</p>
<h3 id="what-function-do-load-generators-in-meshery-provide">
	What function do load generators in Meshery provide?
</h3>
<p>Load generators will provide the capability to run load tests from Meshery. As of today the load generators are embedded as libraries in Meshery and Meshery invokes the load generators APIs with the right load test options to run the load test. At the moment, Meshery supports HTTP load generation. Support for gRPC and TCP load generation is on the roadmap. Meshery has functional integration with fortio, wrk2, and nighthawk.</p>
<h3 id="why-support-multiple-load-generators">
	Why support multiple load generators?
</h3>
<p>Different use cases and different opinions call for different approaches to statistical analysis of the performance results. For example, wrk2 accounts for a concept called Coordinated Omission.</p>
<h3 id="which-load-generators-does-meshery-support">
	Which load generators does Meshery support?
</h3>
<ol>
<li><a href="https://github.com/fortio/fortio">fortio</a> - Fortio load testing library, command line tool, advanced echo server and web UI in go (golang). Allows to specify a set query-per-second load and record latency histograms and other useful stats.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/giltene/wrk2">wrk2</a> - A constant throughput, correct latency recording variant of wrk.</li>
<li><a href="https://getnighthawk.dev/">nighthawk</a> - Enables users to run distributed performance tests to better mimic real-world, distributed systems scenarios.</li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li>See the Nighthawk project.</li>
</ul>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>
