        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Extensibility: Providers</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery offers <em>Providers</em> as a point of extensibility. It has a built-in Local Provider, named <strong>&ldquo;None&rdquo;</strong> and supports <em>Remote Providers</em> that are designed to be pluggable. <em>Remote Providers</em> offer a point of extension to users / integrators to deliver enhanced functionality such as authentication and authorization, using Meshery as a platform.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Extensibility points offer clean separation of Meshery&rsquo;s core functionality versus plugin functionality.</strong>
<ul>
<li>See a list of <a href="https://meshery.io/extensions">Meshery&rsquo;s extensions</a>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Remote Providers should be able to offer custom RBAC, custom UI components, and custom backend components</strong>
<ul>
<li>Dynamically loadable frameworks need to be identified or created to serve each of these purposes.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="what-functionality-do-providers-offer">
	What functionality do Providers offer?
</h3>
<p>The functionalities offerred by a <em>Remote Provider</em> may vary broadly between providers. Meshery offers extension points that Remote Providers are able to use to inject various functionalities, functionalities that are specific to that provider.
Some examples include:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Authentication and Authorization</strong>
<ul>
<li>Examples: session management, two factor authentication, LDAP integration.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Long-Term Persistence</strong>
<ul>
<li>Examples: Storage and retrieval of performance test results.</li>
<li>Examples: Storage and retrieval of user preferences.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Enhanced Visualization</strong>
<ul>
<li>Examples: Creation of a visual cloud native infrastructure topology.</li>
<li>Examples: Different charts (metrics), debug (log viewer), distributed trace explorers.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Reporting</strong>
<ul>
<li>Examples: Using Meshery&rsquo;s GraphQL server to compose new dashboards.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Server Event Management</strong>
<ul>
<li>Examples: Local event storage in database</li>
<li>Examples: Remote event synchronization (Remote providers only)</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<a href="./images/providers.png">
<img src="./images/providers.png" width="50%" /></a>
  <figcaption>Figure: Selecting a provider in Meshery</figcaption>
<h2 id="types-of-providers">
	Types of providers
</h2>
<p>There are two types of providers defined in Meshery, <code>local</code> and <code>remote</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li>The <strong>Local</strong> provider is built-into Meshery.</li>
<li><strong>Remote providers</strong> can be implemented by anyone or an organization that wishes to integrate with Meshery. Any number of Remote providers may be available in your Meshery deployment.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="default-installation-configuration">
	Default Installation Configuration
</h3>
<p>By default, Meshery installations <strong>do not have a provider preselected</strong>. This is an intentional design choice: upon first launch, users are presented with the provider selection UI, allowing them to make an informed choice among all available providers.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Why no default provider?</div>
<p>It might be tempting to preselect the Local provider (&quot;None&quot;) as the default; however, doing so would preclude selection of any other provider by new users who are unaware of other options being available. By leaving the provider unset, all users (whether individual or team-based) are presented with the full range of available providers on first use.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="recommended-production-deployment-settings">
	Recommended Production Deployment Settings
</h3>
<p>For production deployments, consider the following security best practices regarding provider selection:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Do not pre-select a provider</strong> in the default installation configuration. Allow users to choose their provider at startup.</li>
<li><strong>Use a Remote Provider</strong> for production deployments to enforce user authentication and authorization, especially for public-facing Meshery instances.</li>
<li><strong>Enforce a specific provider</strong> using the <code>PROVIDER</code> environment variable only when you have a clear operational requirement to do so, such as locking a deployment to a particular identity provider.</li>
<li><strong>Use <code>mesheryctl system provider set</code></strong> to explicitly configure a provider for a given context when needed.</li>
<li><strong>Use <code>mesheryctl system provider reset</code></strong> to clear an enforced provider and return to the provider selection UI.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="remote-providers">
	Remote Providers
</h3>
<p>The use of a Remote Provider, puts Meshery into multi-user mode and requires user authentication. This provides security for the public-facing Meshery UI as the remote provider enforces identity with authentication and authorization. You should also use a remote provider when your use of Meshery is ongoing or used in a team environment (used by multiple people). This can be seen when using Meshery Playground, where a user is prompted to login through the <em>Meshery Cloud</em> remote provider. Visit <a href="https://playground.meshery.io/">Meshery Playground</a> to experience this.</p>
<p>A specific provider can be enforced in a Meshery instance by passing the name of the provider with the env variable <code>PROVIDER</code>. This applies to both remote and local providers.</p>
<p>Name: <strong>&ldquo;Meshery&rdquo;</strong> (default)</p>
<ul>
<li>Enforces user authentication.</li>
<li>Long-term term persistence.</li>
<li>Save environment setup.</li>
<li>Retrieve performance test results.</li>
<li>Events are stored locally and can be published to remote provider. <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server-events/">Read more about server events</a></li>
</ul>
<h4 id="example-remote-provider">
	Example remote provider
</h4>
<p>Name: <strong>&ldquo;Acme&rdquo;</strong> (default)</p>
<ul>
<li>Enforces user authentication.</li>
<li>Long-term term persistence.</li>
<li>Save environment setup.</li>
<li>Retrieve performance test results.</li>
<li>Events are stored locally and can be published to remote provider. <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server-events/">Read more about server events</a></li>
<li>Free to use.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="local-provider">
	Local Provider
</h3>
<p>The use of the Local Provider, <strong>&ldquo;None&rdquo;</strong>, puts Meshery into a single-user mode and does not require authentication. Use the Local provider when your use of Meshery is intended to be shortlived.</p>
<p>Name: <strong>&ldquo;None&rdquo;</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>No user authentication.</li>
<li>Immediate login - users are redirected directly to the dashboard without authentication prompts.</li>
<li>Container-local storage of test results. Ephemeral.</li>
<li>Environment setup not saved.</li>
<li>No performance test result history.</li>
<li>Server events are stored locally in database. <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server-events/">Read more about server events</a></li>
<li>Free to use.</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="login-behavior">
	Login Behavior
</h4>
<p>When the Local Provider is selected, users are immediately redirected to the Meshery dashboard without any authentication challenges. The login flow for <strong>&ldquo;None&rdquo;</strong> provider:</p>
<ol>
<li>User selects <strong>&ldquo;None&rdquo;</strong> provider from the provider selection UI (or it&rsquo;s enforced via <code>PROVIDER</code> environment variable)</li>
<li>The provider cookie is set and user is redirected to <code>/user/login</code></li>
<li><code>InitiateLogin</code> immediately redirects to <code>/</code> (dashboard) or to the originally requested page if a deep-link was preserved</li>
<li>User begins working with Meshery without any authentication barriers</li>
</ol>
<p>This streamlined flow makes the Local Provider ideal for quick evaluations, demos, and single-user scenarios where authentication overhead is unnecessary.</p>
<h2 id="provider-login-flow">
	Provider Login Flow
</h2>
<p>Understanding how provider selection leads to authentication and dashboard access is important for both users and integrators.</p>
<h3 id="interactive-browser-flow">
	Interactive (Browser) Flow
</h3>
<ol>
<li><strong>Provider Selection</strong>: User visits Meshery and is presented with the provider selection UI at <code>/provider</code> (unless a provider is enforced via the <code>PROVIDER</code> environment variable)</li>
<li><strong>Provider Activation</strong>: User selects a provider → Meshery sets a <code>meshery-provider</code> cookie and redirects to <code>/user/login?provider=&lt;name&gt;</code></li>
<li><strong>Login Initiation</strong>: The <code>/user/login</code> route resolves the provider and calls the provider&rsquo;s <code>InitiateLogin</code> method:
<ul>
<li><strong>For &ldquo;None&rdquo; (Local)</strong>: Immediately redirects to <code>/</code> (dashboard) or to the deep-link target if one was preserved</li>
<li><strong>For Remote Providers</strong>: Redirects to the remote provider&rsquo;s OAuth login page (e.g., GitHub, Google)</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Post-Authentication</strong>: After successful authentication, user is redirected to the dashboard or originally requested page</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="enforced-provider-flow">
	Enforced Provider Flow
</h3>
<p>When the <code>PROVIDER</code> environment variable is set (e.g., <code>PROVIDER=None</code> or <code>PROVIDER=Meshery</code>):</p>
<ol>
<li>Provider selection UI is bypassed</li>
<li>The specified provider is automatically activated and cookie is set</li>
<li>User is redirected directly to <code>/user/login</code></li>
<li>Login flow proceeds as described above based on provider type</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="deep-link-preservation">
	Deep-Link Preservation
</h3>
<p>Meshery preserves the originally requested URL when authentication is required, enabling seamless navigation after login:</p>
<ul>
<li>When an unauthenticated user attempts to access a protected page, the URL is base64-encoded into a <code>ref</code> query parameter</li>
<li>After successful login, the provider decodes <code>ref</code> and redirects to the original destination</li>
<li>The Local Provider supports this functionality, validating <code>ref</code> values to prevent open redirects (absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, and URLs with schemes/hosts are rejected)</li>
<li>If <code>ref</code> validation fails or is absent, users are redirected to the dashboard (<code>/</code>)</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Example</strong>: User visits <code>https://meshery.example.com/extension/meshmap</code> while unauthenticated → redirected to login with <code>ref</code> parameter → after login, automatically returned to MeshMap extension.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Deep-Link Security</div>
<p>Deep-link targets are validated to prevent open redirect vulnerabilities. Only relative paths within the Meshery application are accepted.</p>
</div>
<h2 id="runtime-configuration-options">
	Runtime Configuration Options
</h2>
<p>Meshery provides runtime configuration options to control provider behavior:</p>
<h3 id="provider">
	PROVIDER
</h3>
<p>This environment variable enforces a specific provider, bypassing the provider selection UI. This is useful for:</p>
<ul>
<li>Dedicated deployments where only one provider should be available</li>
<li>Automated environments and CI/CD pipelines</li>
<li>Simplified user experience when provider choice is predetermined</li>
</ul>
<p>Accepted values:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>None</code> - Enforces the Local Provider (no authentication)</li>
<li><code>Meshery</code> - Enforces the Meshery (Meshery Cloud) Remote Provider</li>
<li>Any other registered remote provider name</li>
</ul>
<p>Example: <code>PROVIDER=None</code></p>
<p>When set, users are automatically directed to the specified provider&rsquo;s login flow upon accessing Meshery.</p>
<h3 id="provider_capabilities_filepath">
	PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH
</h3>
<p>This environment variable allows you to specify a local file path to load provider capabilities from a static JSON file instead of fetching them from the remote provider&rsquo;s <code>/capabilities</code> endpoint. This is useful for:</p>
<ul>
<li>Offline development and testing</li>
<li>Environments with restricted network access</li>
<li>Ensuring consistent provider capabilities across deployments</li>
</ul>
<p>Example: <code>PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH=/path/to/capabilities.json</code></p>
<h3 id="skip_download_extensions">
	SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS
</h3>
<p>This boolean environment variable controls whether Meshery downloads and refreshes provider extension packages. When set to <code>true</code>, Meshery will skip downloading extension packages even when new versions are available. This is particularly useful for:</p>
<ul>
<li>Development environments where you want to use locally modified extensions</li>
<li>Deployments where extensions are pre-packaged or managed separately</li>
<li>Reducing startup time and network bandwidth usage</li>
<li>Preventing automatic updates to extension packages</li>
</ul>
<p>Default: <code>false</code> (extensions are downloaded/refreshed)</p>
<p>Example: <code>SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS=true</code></p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Extension downloads occur during:</p>
<ul>
<li>User login (via the TokenHandler)</li>
<li>Provider capability refresh operations</li>
<li>Release channel updates</li>
</ul>
<p>When <code>SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS</code> is enabled, existing extension packages will still be loaded if present, but no new versions will be retrieved.</p>
<h2 id="design-principles-meshery-remote-provider-framework">
	Design Principles: Meshery Remote Provider Framework
</h2>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s Remote Provider extensibility framework is designed to enable the following functionalities:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Pluggable UI Functionality</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Out-of-tree custom UI components with seamless user experience.</li>
<li>A system of remote retrieval of extension packages (ReactJS components and Golang binaries).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Pluggable Backend Functionality</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Remote Providers have any number of capabilities unbeknownst to Meshery.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Pluggable AuthZ</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Design an extensible role based access control system such that Remote Providers can determine their own set of controls. Remote Providers to return JWTs with custom roles, permission keys and permission keychains.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="building-a-provider">
	Building a Provider
</h2>
<p>Meshery interfaces with providers through a Go interface. The Provider implementations have to be placed in the code and compiled together today. A Provider instance will have to be injected into Meshery when the program starts.</p>
<p>Meshery keeps the implementation of Remote Providers separate so that they are brought in through a separate process and injected into Meshery at runtime (OR) change the way the code works to make the Providers invoke Meshery.</p>
<h3 id="verifying-compatibility-with-golang-version-update">
	Verifying Compatibility With Golang Version Update
</h3>
<p>When Meshery is updated to a newer version of Golang, extension providers need to ensure their integrations remain compatible with the updated version. Changes in the Golang version can lead to compatibility issues, so it’s important to update your extension to align with Meshery’s new environment. For a detailed guide on how to verify and address any compatibility issues, refer to this <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/verify-compatibility/">guide on verifying compatibility</a>.</p>
<h3 id="remote-provider-extension-points">
	Remote Provider Extension Points
</h3>
<p>Interwoven into Meshery’s web-based user interface are a variety of extension points. Each extension point is carefully carved out to afford a seamless user experience. Each extension point is identified by a name and type. The following Meshery UI extension points are available:</p>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th><strong>Name</strong></th>
          <th><strong>Type</strong></th>
          <th><strong>Description</strong></th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td>navigator</td>
          <td>Menu Items</td>
          <td>This is supposed to be a full page extension which will get a dedicated endpoint in the meshery UI. And will be listed in the meshery UI’s navigator/sidebar. Menu items may refer to full page extensions.</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>user_prefs</td>
          <td>Single Component</td>
          <td>This is supposed to be remote react components which will get placed in a pre-existing page and will not have a dedicated endpoint. As of now, the only place where this extension can be loaded is the “User Preference” section under meshery settings.</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>account</td>
          <td>Full Page</td>
          <td>Remote Reactjs components (or other) are placed in a pre-existing page and will have dedicated endpoint: <code>/extension/account</code>.</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>collaborator</td>
          <td>Single Component</td>
          <td>This is supposed to be remote react components which will get placed in a pre-existing page and will not have a dedicated endpoint. Currently, placed at the Header component of Mehery UI. Its work is to show active Meshery users under the same remote provider.</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>/extension/&lt;your name here&gt;</td>
          <td>Full Page</td>
          <td>The Provider package is unzipped into Meshery server filesystem under <code>/app/provider-pkg/&lt;package-name&gt;</code>.</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Remote Providers must fulfill the following endpoints:</p>
<ol>
<li><code>/login</code> - return valid token</li>
<li><code>/logout</code> - invalidating token</li>
<li><code>/capabilities</code> - return capabilities.json</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="ui-extension-points">
	UI Extension Points
</h2>
<p>All UI extensions will be hosted under the endpoint <code>&lt;mesheryserver:port/provider&gt;</code>.</p>
<h3 id="userprefs">
	UserPrefs
</h3>
<p>The UserPrefs extension point expects and loads a component to be displayed into <code>/userpreferences</code> page.</p>
<h3 id="navigator">
	Navigator
</h3>
<p>The Navigator extension point loads a set of menu items to be displayed in the menu bar on the left hand side of the Meshery UI.</p>
<h2 id="provider-defined-redirects">
	Provider-Defined Redirects
</h2>
<p>Remote Providers can define custom URL redirects through the <code>redirects</code> field in the capabilities response. This allows providers to dynamically control how certain URL paths are handled by the Meshery server, enabling seamless navigation experiences for users.</p>
<h3 id="how-redirects-work">
	How Redirects Work
</h3>
<p>When Meshery server receives a request for a specific URL path, it checks if the connected Remote Provider has defined a redirect for that path in its capabilities. If a matching redirect is found, the server issues an HTTP permanent redirect (308) to the target URL.</p>
<h3 id="configuring-redirects">
	Configuring Redirects
</h3>
<p>Redirects are defined as a key-value map in the provider&rsquo;s capabilities response, where:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Key</strong>: The source URL path to intercept (e.g., <code>/</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Value</strong>: The destination URL to redirect to (e.g., <code>/extension/meshmap</code>)</li>
</ul>
<p>Example configuration in the capabilities response:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">&#34;redirects&#34;: {
  &#34;/&#34;: &#34;/extension/meshmap&#34;,
  &#34;/dashboard&#34;: &#34;/extension/meshmap/dashboard&#34;
}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="use-cases">
	Use Cases
</h3>
<ol>
<li><strong>Default Landing Page</strong>: Redirect users from the root path (<code>/</code>) to a custom extension page.</li>
<li><strong>Custom Navigation</strong>: Guide users to specific extension pages based on their workflow.</li>
<li><strong>URL Aliasing</strong>: Create shorter or more memorable URLs that redirect to extension endpoints.</li>
</ol>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Note</div>
<p>Redirects are evaluated before serving UI content. Only exact path matches are redirected.</p>
</div>
<h2 id="capabilities-endpoint-example">
	Capabilities Endpoint Example
</h2>
<p>Meshery Server will proxy all requests to remote provider endpoints. Endpoints are dynamically determined and identified in the <em><strong>capabilities</strong></em> section of the <code>/capabilities</code> endpoint. Providers as an object have the following attributes (this must be returned as a response to <code>/capabilities</code> endpoint):</p>

<h4 id="meshery-server-registration">
	Meshery Server Registration
</h4>
<p>Every Meshery server is capable of registering itself with the remote provider, considering that remote provider supports this feature as a capability.
On successful authentication with the remote provider, Meshery server registers itself by sending a POST request to the remote provider through the <code>persist-connection</code> capability. The body of the request should include information so as to uniquely indentify Meshery server and its status.</p>
<p>Example of the request body:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{
  &#34;server_id&#34;: &#34;xxxx-xxxxx-xxxx-xxxx&#34;,
  &#34;server_version&#34;: &#34;vx.x.x&#34;,
  &#34;server_build-sha&#34;: &#34;xxxx-xxxxx&#34;,
  &#34;server_location&#34;: &#34;&lt;protocol&gt;://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;&#34;
}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="configurable-oauth-callback-url">
	Configurable OAuth Callback URL
</h2>
<p>As of the release <code>v0.5.39</code>, Meshery Server has extended its capability to configure the callback URL for connected <em>Remote Providers</em>. This is helpful when you are deploying Meshery behind an ingress gateway or reverse proxy. You can specify a custom, redirect endpoint for the connected Remote Provider.
Let&rsquo;s understand this through an example deployment scenario below.</p>
<h3 id="example-deployment-scenario-meshery-cloud-istio-and-azure-kubernetes-service">
	Example Deployment Scenario: Meshery Cloud, Istio, and Azure Kubernetes Service
</h3>
<p>User has deployed the Meshery behind a Istio Ingress Gateway and the Istio is also behind an Application Gateway (e.g. AKS Application Gateway). Generally, when you use a GitHub Remote Provider for authentication, it redirect the request to the Istio Ingress Gateway FQDN. In this setup, redirection won&rsquo;t be successful because the Ingress Gateway is behind an additional Application Gateway. In this case, you have to define where the request should be redirected once it is authenticated from GitHub.</p>
<p><strong><em>SOLUTION</em></strong></p>
<p>You can define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable while installing Meshery.</p>
<p><strong>Example using Helm</strong></p>
<p>First, construct the URL in the format
<code>https://[CUSTOM_URL]/api/user/token</code></p>
<ul>
<li>Where <code>[CUSTOM_URL]</code> is the URL where <strong>Meshery server</strong> will be or is installed. For example, <code>https://k8s-staging.test.io/</code>.</li>
<li>And <code>api/user/token</code> is the <strong>Auth Endpoint</strong> and is append at the end of your custom URL.</li>
</ul>
<p>So, the final URL would look similar to
<code>https://k8s-staging.test.io/api/user/token</code></p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Note</div>
<p>Callback URL is not the same as Provider URL. In scenarios where Meshery server and Provider is installed on same server, pay attention to paths or subdomains.</p>
</div>
<p>Next, set the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> variable when running the <code>helm install</code>. Below is an example:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --set env.MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://k8s-staging.test.io/api/user/token</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>NOTE</strong></p>
<p>If Meshery server is accessible in a path of the URL such as <code>https://k8s-staging.test.io/meshery</code>, then the callback URL will be <code>https://k8s-staging.test.io/meshery/api/user/token</code>.</p>
<h2 id="managing-your-remote-provider-extension-code">
	Managing your Remote Provider Extension Code
</h2>
<p>Remote Provider extensions are kept out-of-tree from Meshery (server and UI). You might need to build your extensions under the same environment and set of dependencies as Meshery. The Meshery framework of extensibility has been designed such that in-tree extensions can be safely avoided while still providing a robust platform from which to extend Meshery’s functionality. Often, herein lies the delineation of open vs. closed functionality within Meshery. Remote Providers can bring (plugin) what functionality that they want behind this extensible interface (more about Meshery extensibility), at least that is up to the point that Meshery has provided a way to plug that feature in.</p>
<p>Offering out-of-tree support for Meshery extensions means that:</p>
<ol>
<li>source code to your Meshery extensions are not required to be open source,</li>
<li>liability to Meshery’s stability is significantly reduced, avoiding potential bugs in extended components.</li>
</ol>
<p>Through clearly defined extension points, Meshery extensions may be offered as closed source capabilities that plug into open source Meshery code. To facilitate integration of your Meshery extensions, you might automate the building and releasing of your separate, but interdependent code repositories. You will be responsible for sustaining both your ReactJS and Golang-based extensions.</p>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Extensibility: UI</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery UI has a number of extension points that allow you to greatly customize both its functional behavior and visual appearance. These extension points come in different types, and this document describes each type, its example use, best practices to consider, and caveats of which to be aware.</p>
<h3 id="extensibility-customizing-text-based-forms-using-rjsf-custom-component">
	Extensibility: Customizing Text-based Forms using RJSF Custom Component
</h3>
<p>RJSFWrapperComponent provides customizations for RJSF forms, overriding the default behavior of meshery-ui rjsf forms. The <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L66">Rjsf forms are wrapped</a> in this component to receive custom props from a Meshery extension.


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">&lt;RJSFWrapperComponent {...props}&gt;
  &lt;RJSFForm
    isLoading={isLoading}
    schema={schema}
    data={data}
    onChange={(e) =&gt; {
      setData(e.formData)
    }}
    jsonSchema={jsonSchema}
  /&gt;
&lt;/RJSFWrapperComponent&gt;</code>
	</div>
</pre>

See this <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L91">RJSF Component</a> as an example of how these properties are received.</p>
<h3 id="extensibility-user-accounts">
	Extensibility: User Accounts
</h3>
<p>Meshery Server uses <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/providers/">Providers</a> for identity management. Providers can implement the <code>user_account</code> extension to handle custom user management scenarios. The user avatar behavior, which changes based on the user&rsquo;s status, can be customized by extending the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/7de49ef4928f114080f923f2ad261f4433ca91d6/ui/components/User.js#L46">User Component</a>.</p>
<h3 id="build-time-ui-extensibility">
	Build-Time UI Extensibility
</h3>
<p>Meshery offers powerful customization options for its web application user interface at build time. This feature allows developers to tailor the UI to specific needs by modifying component behavior, managing routes, and applying custom themes.</p>
<h5 id="configuration-file">
	Configuration File
</h5>
<p>The build-time UI customization is controlled through the <code>ui.config.js</code> file. This file supports various configuration options to modify the Meshery UI.</p>
<h5 id="current-features">
	Current Features
</h5>
<p><em>Component Management</em></p>
<p>You can control the visibility and behavior of various UI components. For example:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-javascript" data-lang="javascript"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nx">module</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">exports</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">components</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">navigator</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="c1">// Set to false to disable the navigator component (default: true)
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="c1">// Add other components here as needed
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">},</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">};</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><p><em>Upcoming Features</em></p>
<p>Meshery is continuously expanding its UI extensibility capabilities. The following features are planned for future releases:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Route Management</strong>: Ability to disable or modify specific routes.</li>
<li><strong>Redirect Configuration</strong>: Set up custom redirects within the application.</li>
<li><strong>Custom Theming</strong>: Apply custom themes to personalize the look and feel of the Meshery UI.</li>
</ol>
<h4 id="usage">
	Usage
</h4>
<p>To customize the Meshery UI:</p>
<ol>
<li>Locate the <code>ui.config.js</code> file in your Meshery project.</li>
<li>Modify the configuration options according to your requirements.</li>
<li>Rebuild the Meshery application to apply your changes.</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="loading-screen-message-persistence">
	Loading Screen Message Persistence
</h3>
<p>Meshery UI displays a randomly selected loading message while the application and extensions load. To ensure a consistent user experience, the same loading message is displayed across all loading screens (main UI and extensions) during a single session.</p>
<h4 id="how-it-works">
	How It Works
</h4>
<p>The loading message is selected once and stored in the browser&rsquo;s <code>window</code> object (<code>window.__mesheryLoadingMessage</code>). All subsequent loading screens retrieve this persisted message, preventing jarring re-renders with different messages.</p>
<h4 id="using-the-persisted-loading-message-in-ui-plugins">
	Using the Persisted Loading Message in UI Plugins
</h4>
<p><strong>No changes needed</strong> for plugins that:</p>
<ul>
<li>Use <code>DynamicFullScreenLoader</code> (already imports <code>randomLoadingMessage</code>)</li>
<li>Are loaded through the main Meshery UI framework</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>For standalone loaders</strong>, import the persisted message:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-javascript" data-lang="javascript"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">randomLoadingMessage</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="nx">from</span> <span class="s1">&#39;@/components/LoadingComponents/loadingMessages&#39;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1">// or
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">getPersistedLoadingMessage</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="nx">from</span> <span class="s1">&#39;@/components/LoadingComponents/loadingMessages&#39;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1">// Then use in your loading component:
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">LoadingScreen</span> <span class="nx">message</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">randomLoadingMessage</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="o">/&gt;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>The <code>randomLoadingMessage</code> export automatically retrieves the persisted value from <code>window.__mesheryLoadingMessage</code>, ensuring consistency across all loaders in your plugin.</p>
<h4 id="passing-new-custom-prop-to-forms">
	Passing new custom prop to forms:
</h4>
<ol>
<li>Pass the new prop from the Meshery Extension in the RJSF Wrapper component used like this:</li>
</ol>
<p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">function RJSFWrapperComponent(props) {
// Clone the child to pass in additional props
const children = React.cloneElement(props.children, {
...(props.children?.props || {}),
customComponent: YOUR_NEW_CUSTOM_COMPONENT_OR_PROP
});

return children
}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

Extract the props in the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/0bc68d1cd0ba80a565afa68bce80899c22db9a2e/ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/RJSF.js#L91">RJSFForm Component</a></p>
<p><em>Extensibility documentation missing?</em>
Submit an issue to request more documentation.</p>
<h3 id="extension-points-by-file">
	Extension Points by File
</h3>
<ol>
<li><strong>/ui/components/NavigatorExtension.js</strong> - add custom menu items in Meshery&rsquo;s main navigation menu.</li>
<li><strong>/ui/pages/extension/[component].js</strong> - optionally, define the state of a parent menu item: expanded or collapsed.</li>
<li><strong>ui/remote-component.config.js</strong> - list of Material UI components made available to Remote Providers and their plugins.</li>
<li><strong>ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternServiceFormCore.js</strong> - PatternServiceFormCore component which decouples the SettingsForm and TraitsForm from their UI representation while keeping the logic coupled. This design lets the Remote Provider amend the design of the components without interfering with Meshery UI&rsquo;s core logic.</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="using-react-json-schema-form">
	Using React JSON Schema Form
</h3>
<p>Meshery exposes a custom RJSF Form component which is capable of generating &ldquo;Pattern&rdquo; YAMLs without being extremely opinionated about the UI. This custom component is available at <code>ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternServiceFormCore.js</code>. An example usage of the component which will render the logically coupled <code>SettingsForm</code> and <code>TraitsForm</code> in a Material UI <code>TabPanel</code>:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">&lt;PatternServiceFormCore
formData={formData}
schemaSet={schemaSet}
onSubmit={onSubmit}
onDelete={onDelete}
reference={reference}
namespace={namespace}

&gt;

    {(SettingsForm, TraitsForm) =&gt; {
    	return (
    		&lt;div&gt;
    			&lt;TabPanel value={tab} index={0} style={ { marginTop: &#34;1.1rem&#34; } }&gt;
    				&lt;SettingsForm /&gt;
    			&lt;/TabPanel&gt;
    			&lt;TabPanel value={tab} index={1} style={ { marginTop: &#34;1.1rem&#34; } }&gt;
    				&lt;TraitsForm /&gt;
    			&lt;/TabPanel&gt;
    		&lt;/div&gt;
    	);
    }}

&lt;/PatternServiceFormCore&gt;</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Meshery UI&rsquo;s RJSF form accepts two props:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>RJSFWrapperComponent</code>: The wrapper component gets all of the props that are passed to the underlying form, allowing to inspect the props and changing the behaviour based on them.</li>
<li><code>RJSFFormChildComponent</code>: This component will customize the internals of the RJSF form.</li>
</ul>
<p>With both of these props, Remote Providers can customize the wrapper and can also customize the body of the form. This allows full customization of the form.</p>
<p>from <em>ui/components/MesheryMeshInterface/PatternService/index.js</em>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">function PatternService({ formData, jsonSchema, onChange, type, onSubmit, onDelete, RJSFWrapperComponent, RJSFFormChildComponent })</code>
	</div>
</pre>
</p>

        </div>

<script>

        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Ensuring Extension Compatibility with Meshery</h1>
          
          <p>The Meshery ecosystem is designed for extensibility, with the core platform (<code>meshery/meshery</code>) providing extension points for a variety of plugins, collectively managed in the <code>meshery-extensions</code> GitHub organization. To ensure a stable and seamless user experience, it is critical that extensions remain compatible with the Meshery platform, especially when shared frameworks or dependencies are updated.</p>
<p>This guide outlines the key areas of compatibility and provides a general process for extension developers to follow when Meshery&rsquo;s underlying frameworks are updated.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Meshery's Bill of Materials</div>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s version is defined by its <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/#meshery-contribution-flow">Bill of Materials (BOM)</a>, which specifies versions for Go, Node.js, and other key dependencies. Extension developers should reference the BOM to ensure alignment.</p>
</div>
<h2 id="key-areas-for-compatibility">
	Key Areas for Compatibility
</h2>
<p>Compatibility between Meshery and its extensions spans several areas. When the Meshery platform is updated, one or more of the following are likely to change:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Language Runtimes</strong>: Meshery and its extensions are often built using the same programming languages. Ensuring version alignment is the first step to compatibility.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Go Version</strong>: Meshery is primarily written in Go. Extensions written in Go must be compiled with the same major Go version to ensure binary compatibility.</li>
<li><strong>Node.js Version</strong>: UI extensions may depend on the Node.js version used by Meshery&rsquo;s UI.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Shared Go Libraries</strong>: Meshery and its extensions share a common set of libraries (<code>meshery/meshkit</code>) that provide foundational utilities, API clients, and data models.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>MeshKit</strong>: Extensions must depend on the same version of <code>meshkit</code> as the Meshery server to avoid mismatches in data structures and function signatures.</li>
<li><strong>gRPC and Protobuf</strong>: Meshery uses gRPC for communication. Extensions must use the same Protobuf definitions (<code>.proto</code> files) and generated Go code to ensure API compatibility.</li>
<li><strong>Other Dependencies</strong>: Align versions of other critical shared dependencies listed in Meshery&rsquo;s <code>go.mod</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>UI Frameworks and Component Libraries</strong>: UI-based extensions must align with Meshery&rsquo;s frontend technology stack to ensure a consistent user experience and functional correctness.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>React and Next.js</strong>: Align with the versions used in Meshery&rsquo;s UI.</li>
<li><strong>Material-UI (MUI)</strong>: Use the same version of the MUI component library to maintain visual consistency.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Build and CI/CD Tooling</strong>: The build process for extensions should be compatible with the environment and tooling used by Meshery.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Makefiles</strong>: Variables and targets in the core Meshery Makefiles (e.g., <code>install/Makefile.core.mk</code>) may be updated.</li>
<li><strong>Docker Images</strong>: Base Docker images used for building and running Meshery may be updated, affecting the extension&rsquo;s build environment.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="general-process-for-verifying-compatibility">
	General Process for Verifying Compatibility
</h2>
<p>When Meshery&rsquo;s Bill of Materials is updated, follow this general process to verify and update your extension.</p>
<h3 id="1-identify-the-changes-in-meshery">
	1. Identify the Changes in Meshery
</h3>
<p>Start by reviewing the release notes or commit history of the <code>meshery/meshery</code> repository to understand what has changed. Pay close attention to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Go version updates in the root <code>go.mod</code> and <code>install/Makefile.core.mk</code>.</li>
<li>Version changes for <code>meshery/meshkit</code> and other key dependencies in <code>go.mod</code>.</li>
<li>Updates to UI framework versions in <code>ui/package.json</code>.</li>
<li>Changes to <code>.proto</code> files for gRPC services.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="2-update-your-extensions-dependencies">
	2. Update Your Extension&rsquo;s Dependencies
</h3>
<p>In your extension&rsquo;s repository, update your dependency files to match the versions used in Meshery.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>For Go-based extensions</strong>:
<ol>
<li>Update the <code>go</code> directive in your <code>go.mod</code> file to match Meshery&rsquo;s.</li>
<li>Update the required version of <code>github.com/meshery/meshkit</code> and other shared modules:
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-sh" data-lang="sh"><span class="line"><span class="cl">go get github.com/meshery/meshkit@vX.X.X
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">go mod tidy
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
</ol>
</li>
<li><strong>For UI-based extensions</strong>:
<ol>
<li>Update the versions of React, Next.js, MUI, and other relevant packages in your <code>package.json</code>.</li>
<li>Run <code>npm install</code> or <code>yarn install</code> to update your dependencies.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="3-rebuild-and-test-your-extension">
	3. Rebuild and Test Your Extension
</h3>
<p>After updating the dependencies, rebuild your extension to ensure it compiles without errors.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>For Go-based extensions</strong>:
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-sh" data-lang="sh"><span class="line"><span class="cl">go build -o &lt;your-extension-binary&gt;
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
<li><strong>For UI-based extensions</strong>:
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-sh" data-lang="sh"><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm run build
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="4-perform-integration-testing">
	4. Perform Integration Testing
</h3>
<p>Run your updated extension with the latest version of Meshery to verify end-to-end compatibility.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Run the latest Meshery server</strong>. Ensure you are using the build corresponding to the dependency updates.</li>
<li><strong>Run your updated extension</strong>.</li>
<li><strong>Monitor the logs</strong> of both Meshery and your extension for any runtime errors, panics, or warnings related to version mismatches.</li>
<li><strong>Thoroughly test your extension&rsquo;s functionality</strong>. Verify that all interactions with Meshery are working as expected, including API calls and UI integrations.</li>
</ol>
<p>By following this process, you can ensure that your extension remains compatible with the ever-evolving Meshery platform, providing a reliable and consistent experience for all users.</p>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Meshery Adapter for App Mesh</h1>
          
          
<article>
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/extensions/adapters/app-mesh/images/app-mesh.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/extensions/adapters/app-mesh/images/app-mesh-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/extensions/adapters/app-mesh/images/app-mesh.svg" class="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy"/> App Mesh</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-app-mesh">beta</a></td>
    <td>v0.6.4</td>
    <td>v1.4.1</td>
  </tr>
</table>

  <h3 id="features">
	Features
</h3>
<ol>
<li>Lifecycle management of App Mesh</li>
<li>Lifecycle management of sample applications</li>
<li>Performance testing</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="sample-applications">
	Sample Applications
</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/#emojivoto">Emojivoto</a></p>
<ul>
<li>A microservice application that allows users to vote for their favorite emoji, and tracks votes received on a leaderboard.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/#bookinfo">Bookinfo</a></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/#httpbin">Httpbin</a></p>
<ul>
<li>Httpbin is a simple HTTP request and response service.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="performance-management">
	Performance Management
</h3>
<p>Identify overhead involved in running the App Mesh, various App Mesh configurations while running different workloads and on different infrastructure. The adapter facilitates data plane and control plane performance testing.</p>
<ol>
<li>Prometheus integration</li>
<li>Grafana integration</li>
</ol>
<p>The <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-app-mesh">Meshery Adapter for App Mesh</a> will connect to App Mesh’s Prometheus and Grafana instances running in the control plane.</p>
  
  






<h3>Lifecycle management</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for App Mesh can install <strong>v1.4.1</strong> of App Mesh. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for App Mesh.</p>


  <p>The Meshery Adapter for App Mesh is currently under construction (beta state), which means that the adapter is not fully functional. Want to contribute? Check our <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-app-mesh">progress</a>.</p>











</article>

        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

            <h1>Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh</h1>
          
          
<article>
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/extensions/adapters/cilium/images/cilium.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/extensions/adapters/cilium/images/cilium-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/extensions/adapters/cilium/images/cilium.svg" class="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy"/> Cilium</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-cilium">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.2</td>
    <td>v1.10.6</td>
  </tr>
</table>

  <p>The Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh is currently under construction (stable state), which means that the adapter is not functional and cannot be interacted with through the <a href="/installation#6-you-will-now-be-directed-to-the-meshery-ui"> Meshery UI </a>at the moment. Check back here to see updates.</p>
<p>Want to contribute? Check our <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-cilium">progress</a>.</p>
  
  






<h3>Lifecycle management</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh can install <strong>v1.10.6</strong> of Cilium. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh.</p>











    <h3>Install Cilium</h3>
    <p>In Meshery's UI, choose the Meshery Adapter for Cilium.</p>
  <a href="/extensions/adapters/cilium/images/cilium-adapter.png">
    <img style="width:500px;" src="/extensions/adapters/cilium/images/cilium-adapter.png" />
  </a>

  <p>Click on (+) and choose the <strong>v1.10.6</strong> of the Cilium.</p>

  <a href="/extensions/adapters/cilium/images/cilium-install.png">
    <img style="width:500px;" src="/extensions/adapters/cilium/images/cilium-install.png" />
  </a>


</article>

            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Meshery Adapter for Consul</h1>
          
          
<article>
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/consul.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/consul-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/consul.svg" class="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy"/> Consul</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-consul">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.3</td>
    <td>v1.8.4</td>
  </tr>
</table>

  <h3 id="features">
	Features
</h3>
<ol>
<li>Lifecycle management of Consul</li>
<li>Lifecycle management of sample applications</li>
<li>Performance management of Consul and it workloads
<ul>
<li>Prometheus and Grafana integration</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Configuration management and best practices of Consul</li>
<li>Custom configuration</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="sample-applications">
	Sample Applications
</h3>
<p>Meshery supports the deployment of a variety of sample applications on Meshery Adapter for Consul. Use Meshery to deploy any of these sample applications.</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/#httpbin">httpbin</a>
<ul>
<li>Httpbin is a simple HTTP request and response service.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/#bookinfo">Bookinfo</a>
<ul>
<li>The sample BookInfo application displays information about a book, similar to a single catalog entry of an online book store.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/#imagehub">Image Hub</a>
<ul>
<li>Image Hub is a sample application written to run on Consul for exploring WebAssembly modules used as Envoy filters.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="performance-management-of-consul-and-it-workloads">
	Performance management of Consul and it workloads
</h3>
<h4 id="prometheus-and-grafana-integration">
	Prometheus and Grafana integration
</h4>
<p>The Meshery Adapter for Consul will connect to Meshery Adapter for Consul&rsquo;s Prometheus and Grafana instances running in the control plane (typically found in a separate namespace) or other instances to which Meshery has network reachability.</p>
<h3 id="architecture">
	Architecture
</h3>
<p><a href="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/service-mesh-architecture-consul.png"><img class="content-image" src="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/service-mesh-architecture-consul.png" alt="Consul Service Mesh Architecture"  /></a></p>
<h3 id="suggested-topics">
	Suggested Topics
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Examine <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/">Meshery&rsquo;s architecture</a> and how adapters fit in as a component.</li>
<li>Learn more about <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/adapters/">Meshery Adapters</a>.</li>
</ul>
  
  






<h3>Lifecycle management</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Consul can install <strong>v1.8.4</strong> of Consul. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for Consul.</p>











    <h3>Install Consul</h3>
    <p>In Meshery's UI, choose the Meshery Adapter for Consul.</p>
  <a href="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/consul-adapter.png">
    <img style="width:500px;" src="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/consul-adapter.png" />
  </a>

  <p>Click on (+) and choose the <strong>v1.8.4</strong> of the Consul.</p>

  <a href="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/consul-install.png">
    <img style="width:500px;" src="/extensions/adapters/consul/images/consul-install.png" />
  </a>


</article>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

<h2 id="guiding-principles-of-adapter-design">
	Guiding Principles of Adapter Design
</h2>
<p>Adapters allow Meshery to interface with the different cloud native infrastructure. Review the list of all available <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/adapters/">Meshery Adapters</a>. See the <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/">Meshery Architecture</a> diagrams for visuals on how adapters relate to other Meshery components.
Meshery upholds the following guiding principles for adapter design:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Adapters allow Meshery to interface with the different cloud native infrastructure, exposing their differentiated value to users.</strong></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li>Cloud native infrastructure projects should be encouraged to maintain their own adapters. Allowing them to expose their differentiated capabilities encourages this.</li>
</ul>
<ol>
<li><strong>Adapters should avoid wheel reinvention, but seek to leverage the functionality provided by cloud native infrastructure under management.</strong></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li>This both reduces sustaining costs and improves reliability.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="adapter-capabilities">
	Adapter Capabilities
</h3>
<p>Meshery communicates with adapters over gRPC. Adapters establish communication with the cloud native infrastructure. Adapters have a predefined set of operations which are grouped based on predefined operation types.</p>
<p>The predefined operation types are:</p>
<ul>
<li>Install</li>
<li>Sample application</li>
<li>Config</li>
<li>Validate</li>
<li>Custom</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="meshery-adapter-codebase-overview">
	Meshery Adapter Codebase Overview
</h2>
<p><a href="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1uQU7e_evJ8IMIzlLoBi3jQSRvpKsl_-K1COVGjJVs30/edit">Common libraries</a> are used to avoid code duplication and apply DRY.</p>
<h3 id="meshkit">
	<a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit">MeshKit</a>
</h3>
<p>The code hierarchy is pluggable and independent from one another. There can be N number of packages depending upon the use case.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>errors/</code> - holds the implementations and the error handlers and error codes which are used across projects.</li>
<li><code>logger/</code> - holds the implementations of logging handler and custom attributes to add if any.</li>
<li><code>utils/</code> - holds all the utility functions that are specific to meshery projects and are to be used generically across all of them.</li>
<li><code>tracing/</code> - holds the implementations of tracing handlers with different tracing providers like jaeger,newrelic, etc.</li>
</ul>
<p>Each package inside a meshkit is a handler interface implementation, the implementation could be from any third-party packages.</p>
<h3 id="meshery-adapter-library">
	<a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-adapter-library">Meshery Adapter Library</a>
</h3>
<p>This section contains a high level overview of the meshery-adapter-library, its purpose and architecture. For details, the reader is referred to the documentation and the code in the repository.</p>
<p>The main purpose of the meshery-adapter-library is to:</p>
<ul>
<li>provide a set of interfaces, some with default implementations, to be used and extended by adapters.</li>
<li>implement common cross cutting concerns like logging, errors, and tracing</li>
<li>provide a mini framework implementing the gRPC server that allows plugging in the mesh specific configuration and - operations implemented in the adapters.</li>
<li>provide middleware extension points</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="/extensions/adapters/images/meshery-adapter-library.svg"><img class="content-image" src="/extensions/adapters/images/meshery-adapter-library.svg" alt="Meshery Adapter Library"  /></a></p>
<p><em>Figure: Displaying Meshery Adapter library architecture along with an example of integration</em></p>
<h4 id="overview-and-usage">
	Overview and Usage
</h4>
<p>The library consists of interfaces and default implementations for the main and common functionality of an adapter. It also provides a mini-framework that runs the gRPC adapter service, calling the functions of handlers injected by the adapter code. This is represented in an UML-ish style in the figure pictured. The library is used in all of Meshery&rsquo;s adapters.</p>

</article>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>
